```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has a defined, low-cost acquisition path into a marketplace where buyers are already looking: Shopify App Store ads start at $5/day, with one reported CPI about one-third of other ad networks. A relies on Google Ads at a $5.42 average CPC and Product Hunt launches its own brief calls highly variable, competing against dozens of similar products.",
    "B's competitive set looks beatable on execution. Most direct competitors have 0-3 reviews, and Describly's only review is 1-star for reliability and support. A's competitors include Canny and Frill with free tiers, plus a 62-tool pricing study showing a commoditized category.",
    "B has an identified gap left by the free incumbent: Shopify Magic does not handle alt text, images, titles, or bulk editing. A's brief says incumbents already ship AI summarization and agent integrations, which erodes the AI-native wedge it proposes.",
    "B's demand evidence comes from three independent merchant pain statements plus an accessibility-urgency angle. A's demand evidence is two quotes, one of which argues against paying.",
    "A carries extra trust and compliance friction for a one-person vendor: a DPA, GDPR/CCPA obligations, and possible SOC2 expectations for an embedded, data-handling, customer-facing widget. B's brief lists no comparable regulatory setup."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence is thin and partly self-defeating. The pain quote comes from an indie builder promoting their own feedback widget, not from a buyer. The only buyer-side quote, from an older r/SaaS thread, says spending $50-80/month on a feedback widget is 'ridiculous.' That signals price resistance, not willingness to pay.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both niches are saturated, and B has real risks. Shopify Magic gives away basic descriptions for free. Subscriptions may churn once a catalog is processed. The ADA settlement figures come from vendor and content-marketing blogs. The CPI claim rests on a single developer anecdote. B wins mainly on distribution and weak-looking competitors, which matter most for reaching a first paying customer within 90 days."
}
```
